title: coord: coordination-number distributions
purpose: Exercises `coord`, which for each distribution counts the `atom2` atoms within [rmin, rmax] of every `atom1` atom and histograms these coordination numbers, together with the mean bond length for each coordination number [@epsrmanual]. Optionally only `atom1` atoms in a window `rminrmaxc` from a centre type are used, measured in 3D (`atom-c`), along z (`atom-z`) or in the xy-plane (`atom-r`).
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Coordination shells: water-water hydrogen bonds O1···H1 1.4-2.4 Å, water O1 around S 2.5-4.5 Å and DMSO O···water H1 1.2-2.5 Å (`hbond`); O1-O1 2.0-3.4 Å for O1 within 1 Å in z of an O1 (`slabz`); O1-O 1.0-3.5 Å within 3 Å of S in the xy-plane (`cylr`); O1-O1 and O1-H1 coordination of water in the shells 3-5 Å and 2.5-4 Å from S (`centreS`).
inputs: Four keyword files `hbond`, `slabz`, `cylr`, `centreS` `.COORD.dat` (3, 1, 1 and 2 distributions; `slabz` with `nsumt -1`, the others `nsumt 0`); `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: The four commands run in sequence, the list twice, so three inputs accumulate over the two passes. Compared: the four `.COORD.n01` files (histogram and mean bond length columns), the four rewritten `.dat` files and `fort.14` of the last run (`centreS`), whose line uses Fortran format reversion; the reference gives mean coordination numbers 2.593 (rms 1.057) for O1-O1 and 1.058 (rms 0.628) for O1-H1 around S. The README states that `fort.14` of `hbond` (`ltypc = 0` branch) was also checked identical in a separate single-command run. The configuration is the same in every pass, so the chained passes test the read-back of the accumulated file and the running-average arithmetic.
